title: indigo_mount_lx200: MOUNT_STATE slew light does not follow a kept coordinates ALERT; a GoTo handled before the first poll is published OK
description: Audit in 1078b2c4 found the same order defect as in synscan (the light is computed before indigo_update_coordinates()). Second part, approved by the owner for this ticket: on the profiles decoded by meade_update_generic_state() a GoTo handled before the first poll of a session (or after a sync whose readback failed) is published OK by that poll while the mount is still slewing, because last_position_valid is false and there is nothing to compare with (review remark of 82634c3e). Fix by seeding lastRA/lastDec from a position read in meade_init_mount() (one extra round trip at connect) and after a failed sync readback as far as possible, with a simulator case. Owner's rule (decided 2026-11-22 for mount_synscan, ticket 1078b2c4, and extended to this driver on 2026-11-23): whenever MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES is in ALERT, the SLEW light of MOUNT_STATE is ALERT too; BUSY while the coordinates are BUSY; otherwise as before. The library keeps a coordinates ALERT until the next BUSY (indigo_update_coordinates() kept-ALERT rule, indigo_reject_coordinates_change()), so the light must be derived from the coordinates state after indigo_update_coordinates() has decided it, at every place the driver publishes the coordinates or MOUNT_STATE (poll, refusals, sync, abort, park/home, connect), not from the driver's own motion flags alone. Reference implementation: synscan_update_mount_state() and its call order in indigo_drivers/mount_synscan/indigo_mount_synscan.driver (commit 5f794cc15). Scope: the .driver source (version bump, regenerate with the unchanged generator), simulator-backed cases proving the light follows the coordinates state through a refused/failed request (ALERT kept while idle), the next accepted request (BUSY, then OK/IDLE) and connect, adaptation of existing cases that asserted IDLE under a kept ALERT, recorded run with tools/run_driver_test.py, MIGRATION_STATUS count. Refusals inserted by the generator (parked/homing guards) cannot call driver code; if the light lags there until the next poll, record it in the ticket note and do not change the generator.
